rationale: chomp is a small (23 functions, ~6 KB text) game/search program with a few hot recursive cores (make_list, make_wanted, make_play, queens-style search in queens.c), so the table favors FLA and BCF for maximal control-flow resistance while keeping their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights moderate so the selector applies them to the larger, less latency-critical functions (make_list, make_wanted, main) rather than uniformly inflating the hot recursion; SUB and SPLIT are weighted toward high diversity at near-zero risk because they compose cheaply and amplify FLA/BCF confusion; IBR gets a strong security weight to obscure branch targets in the flattened graphs, with a slightly elevated CorrectnessRisk weight to restrain its use on tight recursive loops; ICALL and IGV are enabled with mid-range weights since chomp has relatively few indirect-call sites and globals, giving modest diversity gains for low overhead; overall, SecurityGain and DiversityGain dominate, and the kept-small CorrectnessRisk weights plus the small code size ensure the ~6 KB text stays within an acceptable overhead envelope.
